literal.prompt: Что Pac-Man должен съесть в лабиринте игры 1980 года, чтобы перейти на следующий этап?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The official manual dates Pac-Man's arcade debut to 1980 and states that eating all Pac-Dots advances to the next stage. It describes the other proposed items as part of the same game, but only Pac-Dots are required for progression; correctIndex remains 2.
literalGroups.locator: Bandai Namco Arcade Game Series: PAC-MAN manual, L11-L14; L12 says the game first appeared in arcades in 1980.; L19-L22; especially L21: eat all Pac-Dots to advance to the next stage.

literalGroups.literal: Чтобы перейти на следующий этап, Pac-Man должен съесть все Pac-Dots в лабиринте. Power Pellet ненадолго делает призраков синими и позволяет Pac-Man съесть их.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The manual directly supports both claims: all Pac-Dots are eaten to advance, and a Power Pellet briefly turns ghosts blue so Pac-Man can eat them.
literalGroups.locator: L19-L22; especially L21: eat all Pac-Dots to advance to the next stage.; L24-L27; L26-L27: Power Pellet turns ghosts blue and lets Pac-Man eat them for a short time.

literalGroups.literal: Фрукт появляется после того, как Pac-Man съест определённое количество Pac-Dots, и приносит бонусные очки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The manual says fruit appears after Pac-Man eats a certain number of Pac-Dots and that eating the fruit earns bonus points; the note preserves the unspecified threshold.
literalGroups.locator: L28-L32; L31-L32: fruit appears after a certain number of Pac-Dots and eating fruit gives bonus points.

literalGroups.literal: Если призрак поймает Pac-Man, тот теряет жизнь.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The manual states that Pac-Man loses a life when caught by a ghost. This is an own-option fact and does not claim ghosts are never edible under a Power Pellet.
literalGroups.locator: L21-L22; L22 says being caught by a ghost costs Pac-Man a life.

literalGroups.literal: После определённого количества Pac-Dots появляется фрукт, который приносит бонусные очки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The manual connects Pac-Dots to fruit timing and bonus fruit: after a certain number of Pac-Dots, fruit appears and yields bonus points. This adds a fact about the keyed item beyond the prompt/key.
literalGroups.locator: L28-L32; L31-L32: fruit appears after a certain number of Pac-Dots and eating fruit gives bonus points.

literalGroups.literal: Power Pellet ненадолго делает призраков синими, и Pac-Man может съесть их.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The manual says eating a Power Pellet turns ghosts blue and lets Pac-Man eat them; it explicitly limits the effect to a short time.
literalGroups.locator: L24-L27; L26-L27: Power Pellet turns ghosts blue and lets Pac-Man eat them for a short time.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Плод — реальный предмет лабиринта и правдоподобный выбор, но руководство говорит, что фрукт появляется после некоторого числа Pac-Dots и даёт бонус; он не является условием перехода на следующий этап. Справка точно описывает фрукт. The manual's fruit behavior distinguishes it from the progression requirement; item is plausible because it is an actual edible game object.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Призраки — реальные противники из того же лабиринта, но контакт с ними отнимает жизнь. Это правдоподобный для вопроса об объектах игры, однако их не нужно съесть для перехода; отдельное временное исключение включается Power Pellet. Ghosts are a plausible game entity but the manual says contact costs a life; they do not satisfy the all-items progression rule. The note states a concrete fact about this option.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Broad adult audience familiar with the iconic Pac-Man maze game.
absoluteDifficulty.ground: This tests the game's central, widely recognizable action: clear each maze by eating all Pac-Dots. The Strong describes Pac-Man as making video games a mass cultural phenomenon (supplementary context L199-L208), while the official manual states the rule directly. The distractors are all actual edible/interactable things from Pac-Man, so recognition plus the stage objective lets a general adult audience distinguish the key without specialist history knowledge.
